title: Identity in a GUC: session-state leakage across pooled requests, fail-open/closed, and subject spoofing
issue: RLS policies read the subject from a GUC (request.uid / request.jwt.claims). A session-level SET survives on a pooled server connection and is inherited by the next request; SET LOCAL is erased at COMMIT and leaves '' behind; and any role can overwrite the GUC to impersonate someone else.
symptom: Each query returns the rows visible to the request under test. Correct: 0 for an anonymous request (session_set_then_anon, set_local_then_anon, local_outside_tx, fresh_anon, spoof_org2), the user's own rows for set_local_ok. A non-zero value for an anonymous/spoofing request is a leak; an error is a fail-open-by-crash availability bug.
